title: Compliance + Security One-Pagers Pack (v2) — draft (slide-based)
content:
Purpose
- Field-ready pack of one-pagers to attach during security review + procurement.
- Designed to be sendable as a PDF pack OR individual pages.
- Must align with canonical Confluence pages + approved FAQ/RFP library language.

Design / formatting notes (DES-912 template)
- Single-page each, plain language, no absolutes (avoid “always/never”).
- Footer: “Redwood Inference | Security Enablement | v2.x | Last reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD | Owner: ____”.
- Use consistent “Hosted / Dedicated / Private” comparison table where applicable.
- Mark “Customer-facing” vs “Restricted (NDA)” clearly. (This deck is intended customer-facing; evidence details live elsewhere.)

---
SLIDE 1 — Cover / how to use
Title: Redwood Inference — Compliance & Security One-Pagers (v2)
Subtitle: For security review & procurement (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

How to use (speaker notes / internal guidance)
- Send the full pack when a prospect asks for “security docs”.
- If the customer is early in diligence, start with: SOC 2 posture + Encryption + SSO/RBAC.
- If the customer has a security questionnaire: use the RFP response library for exact wording + point to specific one-pagers.
- For SOC 2 report: follow the evidence sharing process (NDA may be required). Do not attach reports directly.

Included pages
1) SOC 2 posture overview
2) Encryption + key management
3) SSO/SAML + SCIM + RBAC
4) Audit logging overview
5) Data residency overview
6) Data retention controls
7) Shared responsibility by deployment mode (quick reference)

Owner / contact
- Program owner: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance PM)
- Evidence + SOC 2 requests: Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter (GRC)
- Questions: security@redwoodinference.com (route internally via #security-review-help)

Reviewer comments
- Markus Klein (SE) 2026-01-21: “Put ‘how to use’ on cover. AEs ask which page to send first.”
- Michael Grant (Legal) 2026-01-29: “Avoid hard notification timelines; keep contract-dependent.”

---
SLIDE 2 — SOC 2 posture (customer-facing)
Title: Compliance program overview — SOC 2

Key points (approved framing)
- Redwood Inference maintains a formal security program with third-party assessment and continuous controls monitoring.
- SOC 2 reporting is available to qualified customers/prospects upon request and completion of required process (e.g., NDA).
- Scope and details vary by product surface; we can clarify which services/components are in scope for your intended deployment.

What customers typically want to know
- Audit period covered + report type (Type I vs Type II)
- In-scope services and how deployment mode affects boundaries
- Access process and who to contact

What we provide (process-based, not attachments)
- SOC 2 report access via GRC process (request → verify NDA if required → controlled sharing)
- Bridge letter / status letter when applicable (via GRC)
- Summary of control areas (security, availability, confidentiality, etc.)

Deployment mode notes (high-level)
- Hosted: Redwood operates the service; customers manage their app-layer usage and data they send.
- Dedicated: isolated capacity; Redwood manages the managed service components; customer retains responsibilities for their users, prompts, and client-side security.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): more customer control; responsibilities shift depending on architecture; Redwood documents boundary and operational requirements.

Evidence pointers (internal-only note — do not include in exported PDF)
- See internal evidence pointer index (ENG-23344) for SOC 2 artifacts and approved sharing flow.

Reviewer comments
- Olga Petrov (GRC) 2026-02-01: “Replace ‘available upon request’ with ‘available to qualified customers/prospects upon request and completion of required process’.”
- Naomi Feldman 2026-02-03: “Add line: ‘We can confirm scope for Hosted/Dedicated/Private on request’ to prevent misinterpretation.”

Open items
- Confirm latest audit period and report naming (GRC to fill in at export time; do not hard-code dates in slide body).

---
SLIDE 3 — Encryption + key management (customer-facing)
Title: Encryption & key management

Summary
- Redwood encrypts data in transit and at rest using industry-standard encryption.
- Key management options depend on deployment mode and customer requirements.

In transit
- TLS is used for client-to-service communication.
- Service-to-service encryption is used for internal communications where applicable.

At rest
- Data stored by Redwood (where applicable) is encrypted at rest.
- Backups/snapshots (where applicable) follow the same encryption-at-rest principles.

Key management options (by deployment mode)
- Hosted: Redwood-managed encryption keys (standard). Option discussions for customer-managed keys are handled case-by-case for enterprise requirements.
- Dedicated: similar to Hosted, with additional isolation at the compute/pool level; key management specifics are documented during solution design.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): supports customer-managed keys via integration with customer KMS/HSM depending on architecture.

What we do NOT claim
- We do not claim “customer exclusively controls all keys” for Hosted as a default.
- We do not claim that “no customer data is ever stored” (depends on features, logging/telemetry configuration, and customer usage).

Reviewer comments
- Marcus Lin (SecEng) 2026-01-24: “Keep it principle-based; do not imply a specific cloud provider KMS unless explicitly asked.”
- Colin O’Donnell 2026-01-28: “For Private, mention KMS/HSM as ‘supported integrations’ not ‘included’.”

Open items
- Add a one-line callout for “Private: customer networking + security controls remain customer-managed; Redwood provides deployment guidance.”

---
SLIDE 4 — Identity: SSO/SAML + SCIM + RBAC (customer-facing)
Title: Enterprise access controls — SSO, SCIM, RBAC

Summary
- Redwood Console supports enterprise authentication options and role-based access controls to support least privilege.
- Centralized auditability for admin and access-related actions is available via audit logs (see Audit Logging page).

SSO / SAML
- SSO via SAML for Console access (typical enterprise requirement).
- Recommended configuration: enforce SSO for all users; restrict local auth where feasible.

SCIM (where applicable)
- SCIM provisioning support may be available depending on plan/product configuration.
- If SCIM is not enabled for your plan, we provide alternative onboarding/offboarding workflows.

RBAC model
- Roles support separating duties (e.g., billing admin vs org admin vs read-only).
- Principle: least privilege; access is scoped to organization/project/workspace constructs (depending on product setup).

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Hosted/Dedicated: Console is managed by Redwood; customer configures SSO and RBAC.
- Private: auth integration may be deployed into customer environment; final architecture determines exact boundary.

Reviewer comments
- Ethan Park 2026-01-22: “Avoid listing exact role names here; refer to RBAC reference for matrix during questionnaires.”
- Markus Klein (SE) 2026-01-23: “Add a short line: ‘API keys can be scoped/rotated’ if true; otherwise omit.”
- Naomi Feldman 2026-02-03: “Keep SCIM wording as ‘where applicable’ to avoid overcommitments.”

Open items
- Confirm whether to include an explicit “MFA” bullet or handle only in FAQ/RFP responses (Security PM to decide).

---
SLIDE 5 — Audit logging overview (customer-facing)
Title: Audit logging — visibility & traceability

Summary
- Redwood provides audit logs for key administrative and security-relevant actions in the Console/control plane.
- Audit log availability and export options vary by deployment mode and customer plan.

What is logged (categories; non-exhaustive)
- Authentication / access events (e.g., user login events)
- Administrative actions (e.g., role changes, org/project settings)
- API key lifecycle (creation/rotation/revocation) where applicable
- Configuration changes relevant to security posture

Export / integration
- Export mechanisms may include download and/or integration patterns suitable for SIEM ingestion, depending on deployment mode.
- For enterprise integrations, Redwood can provide guidance and sample events.

Deployment mode notes
- Hosted: audit logs available in Console; export options depend on plan.
- Dedicated: similar to Hosted; additional environment-specific logs may be available depending on configuration.
- Private: customer may integrate logs into their own logging pipeline; boundary depends on what runs in customer environment.

Accuracy / roadmap disclaimer
- This page reflects current logging surface area; planned enhancements are not commitments.

Reviewer comments
- Kevin Osei 2026-01-26: “Do not list specific event names unless we’re 100% sure they match UI + schema.”
- Slack recap (#eng-security 1708602201) 2026-01-27: “Be careful with ‘API request content’—we do not want to imply prompt/response is captured in audit logs.”
- Elliot Price (Docs) 2026-02-02: “Add one sentence: audit logs are distinct from performance telemetry; keep the doc clear.”

Open items
- Decide: include a small “What audit logs are NOT” box (e.g., not a full data plane trace, not prompt/response capture) to reduce confusion.

---
SLIDE 6 — Data residency overview (customer-facing)
Title: Data residency — regions & deployment options

Summary
- Redwood offers regional deployment options to support customer data residency requirements.
- Actual data flows depend on deployment mode and customer configuration.

What “data residency” means in practice
- Where inference requests are processed (compute region)
- Where supporting metadata/logs are stored and processed
- What data may be transmitted cross-region for reliability/support purposes (if any)

Deployment mode comparison (high-level)
- Hosted: customer selects supported region(s) where available; some operational telemetry may be processed per Redwood’s standard operations model.
- Dedicated: more control over region + isolation; contract/solution design can specify region constraints.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer controls environment location and networking; customer-defined residency constraints are typically easiest to enforce.

Customer FAQ prompts this page should answer
- “Can you keep all processing in the EU?”
- “Do logs leave the region?”
- “What about support access?”

Reviewer comments
- Lukas Meyer (Field/EMEA) 2026-01-20: “This needs a simple answer for EU customers: ‘We can support EU region deployments; specifics depend on product mode.’ Avoid naming exact regions unless we keep it updated.”
- Olga Petrov 2026-01-31: “Do not claim ‘no cross-border transfers’ unless we can fully prove it for the specific deployment and contract.”

Open items
- Decide whether to name region list in the slide body vs link out to a maintained page. Current recommendation: do not hardcode a region list in a PDF.

---
SLIDE 7 — Data retention controls (customer-facing)
Title: Data retention — defaults & controls

Summary
- Retention practices differ across data types (account data, operational logs, audit logs) and can differ by deployment mode.
- Redwood supports deletion requests and account closure processes; contractual requirements may govern timelines.

Key concepts to define (for customers)
- Inference payload data: prompts/inputs and model outputs
- Operational telemetry: metrics, traces, error logs
- Audit logs: admin/security events (separate from payload)

Defaults (careful wording)
- Redwood’s default retention depends on the product and data type.
- Customers can request details and, where available, configure or limit retention.

Customer controls / options
- Ability to reduce retention of certain log types may be available for enterprise plans.
- Private deployments may allow the customer to control retention more directly within their environment.

Deletion requests
- Redwood supports customer requests to delete customer data as applicable.
- Some records may be retained as required for security, fraud prevention, or legal obligations (where applicable).

Reviewer comments
- Rachel Kim (CS) 2026-01-25: “Renewals keep asking for a simple one-liner: ‘We can support retention requirements; see this page + talk to GRC for specifics.’”
- Naomi Feldman 2026-02-03: “Do not put specific day counts in a PDF draft; keep day counts only in Confluence canonical page where we can update quickly.”
- Michael Grant 2026-02-04: “Add qualifier re: legal obligations and security logging.”

Open items
- Confirm what we can claim about prompt/response retention in Hosted by default (needs alignment with current product behavior + docs). Do not guess.

---
SLIDE 8 — Shared responsibility quick reference (customer-facing)
Title: Shared responsibility by deployment mode (quick reference)

Goal
- Reduce confusion in security reviews by making boundaries explicit.

Table (draft wording)
Hosted
- Redwood: operates service, infrastructure security, baseline monitoring, patching, access controls, platform audit logs.
- Customer: secures their app, manages end users, configures auth/RBAC, handles prompt/data governance, manages client-side key storage and access.

Dedicated
- Redwood: operates the dedicated managed service, infrastructure security within the managed boundary, monitoring/patching.
- Customer: same as Hosted; plus capacity and network requirements agreed in solution design.

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Redwood: provides deployment artifacts and guidance; operates components as contracted; supports updates as agreed.
- Customer: controls environment, networking, cloud account/on-prem infrastructure, and often more of the logging/monitoring stack; exact responsibilities depend on architecture.

Reviewer comments
- Vivek Kulkarni 2026-01-30: “For Private, we must align with the Private deployment boundary doc; don’t oversimplify.”
- Markus Klein (SE) 2026-02-01: “This slide is gold for procurement calls. Keep it short and avoid jargon.”

Open items
- Add a one-line pointer: “For Private, request the architecture-specific responsibility matrix during solution design.”

---
SLIDE 9 — Appendix (internal only; to be removed from customer export)
Title: Internal notes for export + linking

Export checklist
- Remove Slide 9 before exporting PDFs.
- Ensure footers have: version + last reviewed + owner.
- Confirm language matches Confluence canonical pages for:
  - Data residency and retention
  - Audit logging scope + export
  - Incident response wording

Linking / distribution
- Confluence is the canonical source.
- Drive PDF pack is the field package. Avoid attaching raw evidence artifacts.

Evidence requests
- SOC 2 report, pen test summaries, and subprocessor attestations: route through GRC process.

Known gaps (from field feedback)
- Customers ask “Do you train on our data?” → should be handled in Security FAQ + RFP library; not included as a one-pager yet.
- Customers ask “Exact incident notification SLA” → must remain contract-dependent.

Change log (draft)
- v2 draft created 2026-01-17 (Soojin)
- Major edits 2026-02-05: retention/residency language softened; audit logs clarified re: payload vs audit; SOC 2 access phrasing updated.

NEXT STEPS
- Naomi/Olga/Marcus: final wording pass on Slides 2, 5, 7
- Elliot/Docs: confirm public-doc link targets for any referenced pages
- SE team: validate this matches what’s needed for questionnaires + calls

Notes to self (Soojin)
- Keep each slide to <120 words if possible. The FAQ does the heavy lifting; these are quick sends.
- Avoid naming region lists, retention day counts, and event schemas in a static PDF.
